::: {.tut-standfirst}
The home stretch: review the complete result, handle sensitive species and generate the Darwin Core Archive ready to publish on GBIF and SiBBr.
:::

## Preview

In the **Preview** tab, Saíra shows the final table already in Darwin Core vocabulary, with all corrections applied. This is the moment for one last overall check:

- columns carry the correct Darwin Core names;
- required fields are filled in;
- names and coordinates were validated in the previous steps.

```{=html}
<figure class="shot">
  <div class="frame"><span class="ph-label">screenshot · final preview</span></div>
  <figcaption><b>Figure 1.</b> Preview of the dataset in Darwin Core, with completeness indicators per field.</figcaption>
</figure>
```

## What Saíra adjusts at export

When generating the package, Saíra automatically standardizes the dataset so it meets the repositories' expectations:

- **eventDate** converted to ISO format (`YYYY-MM-DD`).
- **Coordinates** with the decimal separator normalized (comma becomes dot).
- **occurrenceID** generated when missing, to guarantee a unique identifier per record.
- **Licenses** abbreviated to the canonical URL (for example, the matching Creative Commons URL).
- **Columns reordered** into the canonical Darwin Core sequence, with unmapped columns appended on the right, preserving their original names.

## Sensitive species

Before publishing, Saíra checks for **threatened taxa** (based on the national Fauna/Flora list from MMA, bundled with the app). For those records, you can choose to **generalize the location** (reduce the precision of the coordinates) or omit it, protecting vulnerable populations without giving up on publishing the data. The precise original coordinates of sensitive records go into a separate file, kept out of the public package.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Sensitive data calls for a conscious decision
Generalizing the coordinates of threatened species is a best practice recommended by GBIF and SiBBr. Assess case by case: the goal is to share knowledge without exposing the species to collection or persecution.
:::

## Generating the Darwin Core Archive

```{=html}
<ol class="steps">
  <li><strong>Review the metadata (EML).</strong>
    <p>Fill in the dataset title, institution, license and responsible parties; they go into <span class="term">eml.xml</span> and describe the dataset to whoever finds it.</p></li>
  <li><strong>Generate the archive.</strong>
    <p>Saíra assembles the <span class="term">.zip</span> package with <span class="term">occurrence.txt</span>, <span class="term">meta.xml</span> and <span class="term">eml.xml</span>.</p></li>
  <li><strong>Download and publish.</strong>
    <p>Download the Darwin Core Archive and send it to your IPT (GBIF/SiBBr) for publication.</p></li>
</ol>
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## What is a Darwin Core Archive (DwC-A)
It is a standardized `.zip` package: a data file (<span class="term">occurrence.txt</span>), a descriptor that says what each column means (<span class="term">meta.xml</span>) and the dataset metadata (<span class="term">eml.xml</span>). It is exactly what global repositories expect to receive.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## A reusable template comes along
The `.zip` also includes a **mapping template** (`mapping_guide_*.txt`): the "your column → Darwin Core term" record of the mapping you did, with no data. Keep it to auto-map future spreadsheets with the same structure, via **Import template** (see [Darwin Core mapping](03-dwc-mapping.qmd)).
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Need a spreadsheet instead of the package?
Besides the DwC-A, Saíra also exports the dataset as `.xlsx` with **every cell forced to text**, preventing Excel from reinterpreting dates, catalog numbers or coordinates. Handy for manual review or for sending to collaborators.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## Export failed or unavailable?
It is almost always an **empty required field** or a pending validation. Check that <span class="term">occurrenceID</span>, <span class="term">basisOfRecord</span>, <span class="term">scientificName</span> and <span class="term">eventDate</span> are filled in, and that the name and coordinate steps left no unresolved items. Saíra indicates what is missing before releasing the download.
:::

## Publishing on GBIF and SiBBr

With the `.zip` in hand, publication happens outside Saíra, usually via your institution's or SiBBr's **IPT** (Integrated Publishing Toolkit). The archive Saíra generates is already in the expected format: just upload it, check the mapping in the IPT and publish.

## Done

You took a raw spreadsheet all the way to a validated Darwin Core Archive. From here, your data can be found, cited and combined with collections around the world. 🐦
